bull.b: The Phase 2 results provide substantive clinical validation for PGN-EDODM1, with biomarker correction accompanied by improvements in several functional assessments. If replicated in later cohorts, this could strengthen the program’s probability of advancing toward registration and support broader value from PepGen’s development platform.

The offering materially increases resources available for ongoing clinical development and general operations. That funding can support execution across the pipeline over the next several quarters, reducing immediate financing pressure while PepGen advances its lead program and evaluates the platform’s broader potential.

PepGen’s proprietary EDO platform targets a central limitation in oligonucleotide medicines: delivering sufficient therapy into relevant tissues. A delivery approach applicable to muscle and the central nervous system could support multiple programs and create a reusable foundation for developing treatments across severe neurological diseases.

bear.b: PepGen has not yet commercialized a product, so its operations currently depend on research progress and external capital rather than recurring sales. Large ongoing losses mean future value remains highly dependent on clinical and regulatory success, while the absence of commercial revenue limits financial resilience.

Persistent cash outflows require PepGen to continually manage funding against clinical spending and operating needs. Although burn improved versus 2025, the continuing magnitude of negative operating and free cash flow can constrain strategic flexibility and increase reliance on future financing before products generate revenue.

The partial clinical hold introduces regulatory uncertainty around the FREEDOM2 program and may complicate the timing or design of continued development. Even with encouraging clinical data, resolving the FDA’s concerns remains important because regulatory restrictions can delay progress and increase development requirements.
